problems.title: A fractional-part equation
problems.question: Solve $\{x+1\}=x+\lfloor-99.9\rfloor$, where braces denote fractional part and the brackets denote floor.
problems.idea: Use the exact domain and split the problem into manageable cases.
steps: The equation becomes x−⌊x⌋=x−100, so⌊x⌋=100. This is equivalent to 100≤x<101.

problems.title: Maximum over a rational-inequality domain
problems.question: The domain of $f(x)=-x^2+x-1$ is the solution set of $(x^2+6x+8)/(-x^2+x-9)\ge0$. Find its maximum there.
problems.idea: Use the exact domain and split the problem into manageable cases.
formulas: The denominator is $-[(x-1/2)^2+35/4]<0$, so the numerator $(x+2)(x+4)$ must be≤0.
steps: The domain is[−4,−2]. The parabola vertex is at x=1/2, so the function increases throughout this domain. Its maximum occurs at x=−2, with value −4−2−1.

problems.title: Areas inside a bisected rectangle
problems.question: In rectangle ABCD, short side AB=4. The A-bisector meets BC at its midpoint K; AK meets BD at M. Find areas ABCD, ABKD, AMD.
problems.idea: Use the exact domain and split the problem into manageable cases.
formulas: Take $A=(0,0),B=(0,4),C=(8,4),D=(8,0)$. Since AK bisects a right angle, K=(4,4), forcing BC=8.
steps: Rectangle are a is 4·8=32. Trapezoid ABKD has parallel bases BK=4 and AD=8 and height 4, so its are a is(4+8)·4/2=24.
AK has equation y=x; BD has equation y=4−x/2. Their intersection is M=(8/3,8/3). Triangle AMD has base AD=8 and height 8/3, so its are a is 8·(8/3)/2.

problems.title: Isosceles triangle from a radius-height ratio
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has perimeter 16 and inradius r equal to 3/8 of its altitude h to the base. Find its are a and circumradius.
problems.idea: Use the exact domain and split the problem into manageable cases.
formulas: With base b and semiperimeter s=8, $r/h=(bh/2)/(sh)=b/16$.
steps: Thus b=6, and each equal side is(16−6)/2=5. The altitude is √(5²−3²)=4, giving are a 12. The circumradius formula R=abc/(4S) gives R=5·5·6/(4·12).

problems.title: Complete the graph of an odd function
problems.question: An odd function on R equals x²+4x for x≤0. Draw its entire graph.
problems.idea: Use the exact domain and split the problem into manageable cases.
formulas: Oddness means $f(x)=-f(-x)$. For x>0, this gives $f(x)=-[x^2-4x]=-x^2+4x$.
steps: Draw the upward-opening branch y=(x+2)²−4 for x≤0; it has vertex(−2,−4) and zeros−4,0. Reflect that branch through the origin to get the downward-opening branch y=−(x−2)²+4 for x>0, with vertex(2,4) and zero 4. Both branches meet at(0,0).
problems.answer: f(x)=x²+4x for x≤0; f(x)=−x²+4x for x>0. The graph is shown in the diagram.

problems.title: Area from two midpoint cevians
problems.question: In parallelogram ABCD, M, N are midpoints of AB, BC. AN and DM meet at K. AB=5, BC=13, BD=12. Find are a NKD.
problems.idea: Use the exact domain and split the problem into manageable cases.
formulas: Triangle ABD has side lengths 5,12,13 and is right-angled at B. Its are a is 30, so the parallelogram are a is 60.
steps: The are a ratio to the parallelogram is half the absolute determinant of N−D=(1,−1/2) and K−D=(2/5,−4/5): (1/2)|−4/5+1/5|=3/10. Multiply by 60.

problems.title: Exactly four roots of a nested absolute equation
problems.question: Find all a for which $|(x+1)^2-2|x+1|-6|=a$ has exactly four real solutions.
problems.idea: Use the exact domain and split the problem into manageable cases.
formulas: Put $t=|x+1|\ge0$. The inner quadratic is $q(t)=(t-1)^2-7$. Each positive t gives two x; t=0 gives only x=−1.
steps: For a<0 there are no solutions. For a≥0, q(t)=a gives t=1+√(7+a), always positive. The equation q(t)=−a gives t=1±√(7−a), when a≤7.

At a=0 the two equations duplicate one another, giving only 2 x. For 0<a<6, exactly one root from each equation is positive, giving 4 x. At a=6 the extra root t=0 gives 5 x. For 6<a<7 there are 3 positive t, giving 6 x. At a=7 the two inner roots merge at t=1, giving 4 x. For a>7 only the outer positive t remains, giving 2 x.
